newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian copper prices to remain firm next week.
newsitem.headline: Indian copper prices to remain firm next week.

text.p: Indian copper is expected to remain firm in the coming week in line with the uptrend on the London Metals Exchange (LME), dealers said on Wednesday.

"LME prices have gone up in the last few days because of dwindling global inventories. In fact, imported copper is dearer than the locally produced metal," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metals Exchange.

There were no takers for imported copper at 140 rupees per kg against the Indian price of 125-130 rupees per kg for supplies offered by the state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) and the private sector Sterlite Industries.
"I expect the local prices to stay steady to firm," Parikh said. "But I also expect trading volumes to be low."
He said industrial users were directly buying from HCL and Sterlite because of lower prices instead of depending on the trade for their requirements.
Dealers said the demand for metals in India has been dull because of an industrial recession and a liquidity crunch.
"At the moment, users have a lot of material with them. Poor demand in electrical and automobile industries has affected trade," said metals dealer Jashubhai Gangadas Mehta.

Mehta said the non-ferrous metals industry and trade would look forward to the national budget for 1997/98 (April/March) for measures that could help lift the Indian economy from recession. The budget is due on February 28.
Zinc and lead rose by 50 rupees each to 6,550 rupees per quintal (100 kgs) and 4,450 rupees per quintal during the week.
Tin and nickel also gained 100 rupees each to 34,600 rupees per quintal and 36,900 rupees in the same period.
